readinessIndicator.label: Website Readiness Indicator
readinessIndicator.description: Preliminary indicator of observable public website indicators. Reconstructed from active session audit benchmark.

scopeAndTestingConditions.browserContext: Headless Chromium / Automated Safe Crawler V1
scopeAndTestingConditions.geographicAssumption: Origin: India (IN IP range / Mumbai gateway)
scopeAndTestingConditions.initialConsentState: Fresh user session with no prior cookies or local storage
cannotTestScope: Internal data mapping and CRM pipelines behind customer portals
Employee access controls and role-based permissions
Sub-processor agreements, contracts, and transfer mechanisms
Data retention schedules and automated purging scripts
Database encryption-at-rest and internal backup integrity

findings.title: Privacy notice link not found near a public contact form
findings.observedEvidence: Name, work email, phone number, and message input fields detected inside <form id="contact-us">. No hyperlink pointing to privacy policy found within or adjacent to form container.
findings.whyItMatters: Users should be able to understand how information submitted through a website may be handled prior to providing personal data.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a clearly visible privacy-notice link directly near the submit action and review the purpose explanation.
findings.limitation: A public scan cannot verify backend processing, contracts, retention, or internal procedures.

findings.title: Marketing tracking scripts observed prior to user consent interaction
findings.observedEvidence: Initial network requests observed to Google Tag Manager, Meta Pixel (connect.facebook.net), and Hotjar (static.hotjar.com) on clean initial load without cookie banner interaction.
findings.whyItMatters: Tracking and advertising scripts capturing visitor interactions should be evaluated to determine appropriate consent workflows.
findings.suggestedFix: Review script loading configuration so non-essential tracking scripts execute only after explicit user preference selection.
findings.limitation: A public scan can observe initial client-side network calls, but cannot determine backend tag manager triggers or conditional regional exemptions.

findings.title: Consent banner does not provide observable granular or reject control on initial interface
findings.observedEvidence: Detected banner widget container contains only an "Accept All" button and close icon ("X"). No "Reject" or granular preference button observed in primary viewport.
findings.whyItMatters: Under privacy frameworks, consent mechanisms must offer unambiguous and genuine choice to data principals.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a distinct decline/reject option with equal visual weight and a granular category configuration link.
findings.limitation: Scanner cannot determine if consent logic changes based on IP geolocation or returning session tokens.

findings.title: Unclassified third-party analytics script detected on registration page
findings.observedEvidence: Observed external script request to "trk-pulse.cdn-analytics7.net/collector.js". Domain is not in standard known vendor directories.
findings.whyItMatters: Data fiduciaries should maintain full visibility over every third-party script operating on personal data collection pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Identify the vendor operating this domain, verify data transmission payloads, and update internal inventory.
findings.limitation: Scanner does not inspect minified payload payloads or execute proprietary backend tracking APIs.

findings.title: Relevant privacy notice text detected in public footer
findings.observedEvidence: Footer link found on all 14 discovered pages. Privacy policy loaded successfully with 1,840 words. Relevant keywords detected: personal data, rights, retention, contact, grievance officer.
findings.whyItMatters: Providing an easily accessible, functioning privacy notice is a foundational transparency obligation.
findings.suggestedFix: Schedule periodic review with a privacy legal specialist to verify whether actual operational practices align with written terms.
findings.limitation: Language detection does not verify legal sufficiency, accuracy, or operational compliance.

findings.title: Grievance redressal mechanism contact detected in privacy policy
findings.observedEvidence: Found email identifier "grievance@demo-saas.in" and designated title "Grievance Redressal Officer" in section 8 of privacy notice.
findings.whyItMatters: Data principals must have a designated point of contact to register complaints and exercise rights.
findings.suggestedFix: Ensure published grievance email inbox has monitored response workflows adhering to statutory turnaround times.
findings.limitation: Public scan cannot test whether complaints sent to this email receive timely responses.

findings.title: Child-directed cues not detected on primary SaaS pages
findings.observedEvidence: No educational, minor, child, or school-oriented keywords found in metadata or body text across inspected public pages.
findings.whyItMatters: Section 9 imposes heightened obligations including verifiable parental consent and prohibition of tracking for minors.
findings.suggestedFix: Confirm internally whether SaaS platform accounts are restricted strictly to adults or corporate entities.
findings.limitation: Absence of visible cues on public pages does not determine whether users under 18 can sign up or access the application.

findings.title: Sign-up page distinguishes required from optional input fields
findings.observedEvidence: Form fields have visible asterisks and aria-required="true" tags on mandatory fields (Email, Password), while Phone Number is marked "(Optional)".
findings.whyItMatters: Clear differentiation helps users understand necessary versus optional disclosures.
findings.suggestedFix: Maintain clear distinction and ensure optional data is not treated as mandatory during processing.
findings.limitation: Scanner cannot determine if backend APIs reject requests when optional fields are empty.

findings.title: HTTPS enforced with valid HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect
findings.observedEvidence: HTTP port 80 request responded with HTTP 301 redirect to https://demo-saas.in with valid TLS certificate.
findings.whyItMatters: Transport encryption protects data in transit between browser and web server.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) response header to prevent downgrade attacks.
findings.limitation: HTTPS presence does not prove backend system security, database encryption, or secure API architecture.

forms.observedEvidence: Form action points to /api/lead-capture. Fields collected include personal identifiers with no inline notice.
Contains text "By signing up you agree to our Terms and Privacy Policy" with hyperlinks.
Collects enterprise lead information; generic submission button "Book Demo".

unassessableItems.reason: Protected by authentication credentials. Scanner strictly avoids accessing private boundaries.
unassessableItems.humanReviewRecommendation: Evaluate portal data collection, sub-processors, and export features through an in-depth human assessment.

unassessableItems.reason: Network APIs receive form submissions but their storage, retention period, and cloud location cannot be observed publicly.
unassessableItems.humanReviewRecommendation: Conduct internal architecture and data inventory review.
